claims.text: Nanoscale structural disorder and the magnetic phase transition jointly govern the magnetocaloric response of as-deposited, non-equiatomic FeMnNiGeSi-type thin films or nanoribbons.
Nanoscale structural disorder and the magnetic phase transition jointly govern hysteresis in these low-dimensional alloys.
The degree of structural disorder modulates the sharpness of the magnetic phase transition.
The degree of structural disorder modulates the reversibility of the magnetic phase transition during low-field magnetic-cooling cycles.
Annealing below the bulk recrystallization threshold will reduce nanoscale structural disorder.
Such sub-recrystallization annealing can reduce disorder without inducing significant grain growth.
Annealing-induced reduction of structural disorder will sharpen the magnetic phase transition.
Annealing-induced reduction of structural disorder will facilitate more cooperative magnetic-domain reorientation.
Annealing-induced reduction of structural disorder will lower energy barriers to phase reversibility.
Lower energy barriers and more cooperative domain reorientation will decrease hysteresis.
Post-annealed films or nanoribbons will have a larger isothermal entropy change than the as-deposited baseline under identical low-field cycling conditions.
Post-annealed films or nanoribbons will exhibit less hysteresis than the as-deposited baseline under identical low-field cycling conditions.
The proposed behavior applies during magnetic-cooling cycles from 10 to 100 K with maximum applied fields of 1 T.
The hypothesis is applicable to films or nanoribbons thinner than 100 nm when annealing remains below the alloy's bulk recrystallization threshold.
